text:
Predicates:
Listed(x) ::: x is listed in Yelp's recommendations.
NegativeReviews(x) ::: x has received many negative reviews.
Rating(x, y) ::: x has a rating of y.
TakeOut(x) ::: x provides take-out service.
Popular(x) ::: x is popular among local residents.
HamdenPlazaSubway ::: The Hamden Plaza Subway store.
Premises:
∀x (Listed(x) → ¬NegativeReviews(x)) ::: If a restaurant is listed in Yelp's recommendations, then the restaurant has not received many negative reviews.
∀x (Rating(x, y) ∧ y > 4 → Listed(x)) ::: All restaurants with a rating greater than four are listed in Yelp's recommendations.
∃x (¬TakeOut(x) ∧ NegativeReviews(x)) ::: Some restaurants that do not provide take-out service receive many negative reviews.
∀x (Popular(x) → Rating(x, y) ∧ y > 4) ::: All restaurants that are popular among local residents have ratings greater than four.
Rating(hamdenPlazaSubway, y) ∧ y > 4 ⊕ Popular(hamdenPlazaSubway) ::: The Hamden Plaza Subway store has a rating greater than four, or it is popular among local residents.
Conclusion:
¬TakeOut(hamdenPlazaSubway) ::: The Hamden Plaza store does not provide take-out service.
